label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Ecommerce business SSS almost triples footprint at Indurent Park Burton
summary: Super Smart Service (SSS) has signed a 15-year lease on the 175,356 sq ft Unit B173 at Indurent Park Burton, West Midlands, nearly tripling its presence on the park. The unit is EPC A+ and targeting BREEAM Excellent. Indurent says SSS has taken around 1.75m sq ft of UK space this year.
key_figures: 175,356 sq ft; 15-year lease; c.1.75m sq ft taken by SSS in 2026; rent not disclosed
relevance: Big-box take-up by e-commerce on new-build, A-rated stock at a Midlands logistics hub.
why_matters: One occupier taking about 1.75m sq ft in a year is a material share of UK big-box demand. It supports the case for new-build Grade A space on M6/M1 corridors, which the North West competes for, even as investment yields soften.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Glencar progresses construction of bulk storage development for Peel Ports Group
summary: Contractor Glencar is building two bulk storage warehouses, Alexandra Warehouses 6 and 7, at Alexandra Dock, Liverpool, for Peel Ports Group. They will provide 131,730 sq ft of internal storage within a wider 249,529 sq ft development including infrastructure and access works, with about 60,000 tonnes of dry-bulk capacity.
key_figures: 131,730 sq ft storage; 249,529 sq ft wider development; c.60,000 tonnes capacity
relevance: Port-centric supply adds to constrained Merseyside warehouse stock; owner-occupier development rather than investment stock.
why_matters: It is new North West supply above 100,000 sq ft at a time when the region is short of Grade A space. Port-centric storage can relieve inland demand on the M62/M6 corridors, but it is operational space for Peel's own use, not lettable investment stock.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Aviva tables revised plans for 400,000 sq ft Manchester industrial
summary: Aviva has submitted revised plans for 400,000 sq ft of industrial space in five units on the former Ferranti factory at Styal Road and Simonsway, near Manchester Airport. A 2023 scheme was refused over Green Belt encroachment and airport safety concerns; the new design has been changed following consultation earlier this year. (Earlier coverage, included in this first news edition.)
key_figures: 400,000 sq ft across 5 units; site near Manchester Airport; 2023 application refused
relevance: Potential large-scale institutional-backed supply in the South Manchester / M56 market.
why_matters: If approved, this would be one of the largest institutional industrial schemes in Greater Manchester, adding supply to the tight M56 airport sub-market. Its progress will test planning risk for industrial schemes near Green Belt and airport safeguarding zones.

label: FINANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
headline: SevenCitiesLdn wins £163m loan against Victoria Street office
summary: SevenCitiesLdn has secured a £163m senior whole loan from Patron Capital to support its £211m acquisition and repositioning of 123 Victoria Street, a fully let 244,000 sq ft office bought from Landsec. The facility comprises a £148m acquisition tranche and £15m for refurbishment, at 70% loan-to-cost and 59% loan-to-projected value.
key_figures: £163m loan; £211m purchase; 244,000 sq ft; 70% LTC; 59% LTV (projected)
relevance: Evidence that large-ticket office debt is available, from private credit at relatively high leverage.

label: NORTH WEST INDUSTRIAL
headline: Langtree hands over final £25m phase at Hollinwood Junction
summary: Russell WBHO has completed 192,000 sq ft of industrial space at Hollinwood Junction, Oldham (M60), forward-funded by Indurent and delivered by Langtree with Oldham Council. The £25m final phase comprises 13 units from about 5,000 sq ft to 42,000 sq ft. (Earlier coverage, included in this first news edition.)
key_figures: 192,000 sq ft; 13 units, 5,000–42,000 sq ft; £25m phase; forward-funded by Indurent
relevance: New multi-let supply in Greater Manchester; forward funding shows institutional appetite for small/mid-box.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: L&G and Verdion get green light for £30m Greenwich logistics hub
summary: Legal & General's Industrial Property Investment Fund and Verdion have won consent for LiteHub Greenwich, a £30m multi-let scheme of 78,986 sq ft in six units of 5,555–16,000 sq ft on a 2.6-acre brownfield site in West Thamesmead. Completion is targeted for Q4 2027, aiming for BREEAM Excellent and EPC A+.
key_figures: 78,986 sq ft; 6 units 5,555–16,000 sq ft; £30m; 2.6 acres; ready Q4 2027
relevance: Institutional capital continuing to back speculative urban multi-let development.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Padrock secures 71,530 sq ft letting of south-east London warehouse
summary: Padrock has let Erith Logistics Hub, a 71,530 sq ft single-unit development in south-east London, to tabletop manufacturer Nevilles on a 15-year lease. Nevilles will move from its existing Erith premises in April and use the unit as its headquarters and global distribution centre. Padrock described the market as challenging.
key_figures: 71,530 sq ft; 15-year lease; occupation April 2027; rent not disclosed
relevance: Long-lease letting of speculative London mid-box space; occupier relocating locally.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: London leads European investment despite slow recovery, PwC and ULI find
summary: PwC and ULI's Emerging Trends in Real Estate Europe survey of 1,498 professionals keeps London top of the city rankings, but expects recovery to be slower and uneven. Only 45% expect higher profitability in 2027 (50% last year). Construction costs (58%) and interest rates (55%) are the leading concerns for 2027.
key_figures: 1,498 respondents; 45% expect profit growth in 2027 (50% prior); construction costs cited by 58%; interest rates by 55%
relevance: Sentiment indicator: investor confidence softening as rates and build costs bite.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Seneca acquires Lawnswood Business Park in Leeds
summary: Seneca Property has bought the 150,000 sq ft Lawnswood Business Park, north Leeds, for an undisclosed sum; it was marketed at a £20m guide. The vendor, Hillview Real Estate, paid £26.5m in 2018. The park is 81% let to 17 tenants and will be refurbished into smaller fitted suites.
key_figures: 150,000 sq ft; guide £20m vs £26.5m paid in 2018; 81% occupied; 17 tenants
relevance: Regional out-of-town office pricing evidence: c.25% below 2018 price on guide basis.

label: OFFICES
headline: Office owner-occupancy reaches decade high, says Carter Jonas
summary: Carter Jonas research shows owner-occupiers took 13.4% of UK office sales by transaction count in 2025, a decade high. Outside London the share rose to 17.8% (2024 to September 2026) from 13.4% (2018–23); in London from 8.5% to 10.6%. It attributes the shift to lower capital values alongside rising rents.
relevance: Repriced regional offices are attracting owner-occupier buyers, adding liquidity below institutional lot sizes.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Birmingham's £2.2bn Ladywood regeneration plans axed over viability pressures
summary: Berkeley Group and Birmingham City Council have terminated the development agreement for the £2.2bn Ladywood Estate regeneration, a 148-acre, 20-year scheme for more than 10,000 homes. They cite increased construction and regulatory costs and a more challenged housing market and economy as putting significant pressure on viability.
key_figures: £2.2bn; 148 acres; 10,000+ homes; c.20% affordable; 20-year programme
relevance: Viability failure on a flagship scheme; cost inflation is breaking development appraisals.
why_matters: When a developer of Berkeley's scale walks away on viability, it shows that build costs and rates are breaking long-dated appraisals. The same pressures apply to speculative industrial schemes: exit yields are drifting out while costs stay high, so more projects will need pre-lets or forward funding to proceed.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: Richborough Commercial secures major appeal win on M42 corridor scheme
summary: Richborough Commercial has won outline consent at appeal for up to 700,000 sq ft of B2/B8 floorspace near M42 Junction 9 in North Warwickshire, after appealing against non-determination of a June 2024 application. Richborough says it is the first appeal allowing a major industrial and logistics scheme on grey-belt land since the revised NPPF in August. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: Up to 700,000 sq ft B2/B8; M42 J9; outline consent on appeal; grey-belt land
relevance: Planning precedent for logistics on grey-belt land.
why_matters: A first grey-belt appeal win for logistics could unlock land supply around constrained cores, including Green Belt-heavy Greater Manchester and Cheshire. That raises land-value expectations for promoters but should, over time, ease the supply shortage that has supported North West rents.

label: UK INDUSTRIAL
headline: BARJANE submits plans for 420,000 sq ft DHL warehouse
summary: BARJANE has applied for a 420,000 sq ft logistics scheme at Ansty, Coventry, next to Frasers Group's approved 3.3m sq ft headquarters. DHL Supply Chain has agreed to occupy the BREEAM Outstanding, EPC A warehouse if planning permission is granted, giving the scheme a conditional pre-let at the M6/M69 junction. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: 420,000 sq ft; conditional pre-let to DHL Supply Chain; Ansty, Coventry; BREEAM Outstanding target
relevance: Large-format 3PL demand being met by pre-let development rather than existing stock.
why_matters: Big-box demand is turning into pre-let development rather than speculative space. This is the route North West schemes above 300,000 sq ft are likely to need while exit yields sit at 5.50%+.

label: PROPERTY INVESTMENT
headline: Custodian REIT acquires £11m portfolio from syndicated investment vehicles
summary: Custodian Property Income REIT has bought eight fully let retail and industrial properties, mainly in the East Midlands, for £11m from syndicates managed by Lincoln Property Syndicates. The £800,000 rent reflects a 6.7% net initial yield and 7.2% reversionary yield, funded largely by issuing 10.6m new shares plus £400,000 cash. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: £11m; 8 assets; NIY 6.7%; reversionary yield 7.2%; WAULT 6 yrs; avg lot £1.4m
relevance: Pricing evidence for small-lot regional industrial/retail: c.6.7% NIY.

label: OFFICES
headline: Criterion snaps up New London House for 500-room hotel conversion
summary: Criterion Capital's Zedwell Hotels has bought New London House, an 89,722 sq ft office on Fenchurch Street in the City, from Whitbread for an undisclosed sum, and plans to convert it into a 509-room hotel. Zedwell says it targets structurally sound, well-located buildings where conversion unlocks value. (Published before the last briefing but not previously reported.)
key_figures: 89,722 sq ft office; 509-room hotel conversion; price undisclosed
relevance: Continued removal of secondary City office stock via change of use.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Bolton pursues legal challenge into national planning changes
summary: Bolton Council has complied 'under protest' with the National Scheme of Delegation, which makes planning officers the default decision-makers for most applications. It voted to cost a judicial review and to write to all English planning authorities seeking a coordinated legal challenge against the government.
key_figures: Applies to most planning applications; judicial review being costed
relevance: Planning-process uncertainty in Greater Manchester; delegation should speed routine industrial consents if upheld.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: £2bn Manchester-Sheffield tunnel gets funding boost
summary: Future Works Infrastructure's Trans-Pennine Connect, a proposed 14-mile tolled dual carriageway with a tunnel between Manchester and Sheffield, has received £500,000 from the UK Dynamism Fund for feasibility work. The scheme, estimated at £2bn, would be funded by tolls and private or local-authority investors rather than central government.
key_figures: £500,000 feasibility funding; 14-mile route; c.£2bn estimated cost
relevance: Long-term trans-Pennine connectivity for logistics east of Greater Manchester; early-stage only.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: B&Q to cut 63,000 sq ft in Bolton as it looks to right-size
summary: BNP Paribas has applied to subdivide B&Q's 137,000 sq ft Kay Street store in Bolton into three units, cutting B&Q's space by 63,000 sq ft. Aldi would take a new 20,000 sq ft store, relocating from Higher Bridge Street, using space currently occupied by B&Q's Trade Point facility.
key_figures: 137,000 sq ft store; B&Q to give up 63,000 sq ft; 20,000 sq ft Aldi
relevance: Retail-warehouse right-sizing in Greater Manchester; large-box space being recycled to discount food.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Mansell collapsed with debts of £4.2m
summary: An administrator's report from RSM shows Oldham-based off-site construction specialist Mansell Building Solutions collapsed with debts of £4.2m, including £1.3m owed to NatWest. It entered administration in August after 36 years, citing the cost of relocating its headquarters to Oldham, Covid's impact on revenues and planning delays. Creditors include steel-framing supplier Voestalpine Metsec (£550,000).
key_figures: Debts £4.2m; £1.3m owed to NatWest; Voestalpine Metsec £550,000; CCF £220,000
relevance: Supply-chain fragility in North West construction; contractor insolvency risk for developers.

label: PLANNING / DEVELOPMENT
headline: Meanwhile use put forward ahead of £250m Crompton Place regen
summary: Bolton Council plans street-food markets, a big screen and an urban garden on the Victoria Square frontage of the former Crompton Place shopping centre once it is demolished, as MEPC (part of Federated Hermes) leads a £250m regeneration. CBRE and Chapman Taylor designed the meanwhile-use strategy to keep the area active during redevelopment.
key_figures: £250m regeneration; MEPC/Federated Hermes; meanwhile use by CBRE and Chapman Taylor
relevance: Institutional-backed town-centre regeneration in Greater Manchester; retail space being repurposed.
